title: Connection surge (capacity maxed)
summary: A burst of application connections fills the server's connection slots: the runner opens a few connections a second until only headroom slots stay free below max_connections, fills that headroom for a few seconds at most so overshoot more attempts are past the limit, which the server refuses as too many connections, frees the headroom again, and holds the rest (each pings now and then, so most sit idle). It releases them all, pauses, and repeats until the run ends. PostgreSQL (T4) only.

concurrency.description: Connections opened per second while a wave ramps up.

intensity.description: How often each held connection pings: every 15 seconds at 1, every second at 10.

notes.T4: The template sets max_connections to 50 on every T4 size (Standard_B1ms's own default; ADR 0019, 2026-11-03), 35 of them for the runner after the 15 reserved ones, so every size refuses the overshoot. superuser_reserved_connections and reserved_connections are never used, and the headroom only for a few seconds at most, so reset and an administrator can still connect; the other T4 lanes retry a refusal they meet meanwhile.

headroom.description: Connection slots left free below max_connections, after the reserved ones, while a wave holds its connections. A wave that overshoots fills them for 5 seconds at most, then frees them again.

overshoot.description: Connection attempts past the limit in each wave, once the headroom is filled; the server refuses them as too many connections (SQLSTATE 53300, never a failed sign-in), which Database Hub counts as failed connections. Fixed caps, whatever this is set to: at most 5 refused attempts in any minute and 30 in a run; a sign-in failure ends the surge.

maxConnections.description: A hard cap on the connections a wave holds, whatever the server allows.

holdSeconds.description: How long each wave holds its connections (never past the run's deadline).

expectedHubSignals.signal: T4: Connections (active_connections) climbs to the server's limit each wave
T4: Failed connections (connections_failed) above 0 while a wave overshoots
T4: Sessions By State (sessions_by_state) idle jumps; TCP Connection Backlog (tcp_connection_backlog) may rise
expectedHubSignals.note: PostgreSQL enhanced metrics, in the Azure portal's Metrics; Hub's PostgreSQL dashboard shows connections and failed connections.

expectedSymptoms: The server's connection count reaches max_connections minus the reserved slots and headroom
New connections from applications fail with 'remaining connection slots are reserved' or 'too many clients' (SQLSTATE 53300)
Most surge sessions sit idle; CPU stays low, so the bottleneck is connection capacity, not compute
Connections drop back to the baseline between waves
queryLevelEvidence: ContosoCare.Workload status --target T4: connections against max_connections, sessions by state
pg_stat_activity grouped by application_name and state shows the ContosoCare.Demo/connection-surge sessions
demo.scenario_run_events records each wave's size and the refused attempts
reset: Every surge connection closes when the run ends or stops; reset ends any leftover ContosoCare.Demo/connection-surge session with pg_terminate_backend. Nothing is written.
